title: Trump: Mass murder enthusiast shoots 26 people at Ohio bar
description_short: Trump: Mass murder enthusiast shoots 26 people at Ohio bar
description_medium: On August 4, 2019, 24-year-old Conner Betts opened fire outside a bar in Dayton, Ohio, killing nine people and injuring 17. The TrumpFile account says the attack lasted about 32 seconds and investigators found no political or racial motive, describing Betts as drawn to the idea of a mass shooting. The account does not connect the attack to Trump.

title: Ivana Trump Physical and Sexual Abuse During Marriage
description_short: Ivana Trump Physical and Sexual Abuse During Marriage
description_medium: According to The New Yorker, Ivana Trump’s 1990 divorce deposition described an encounter with Donald Trump as rape; Trump denied the allegation. In a 1993 clarification, she said she had used “rape” to describe feeling violated and did not mean it literally or criminally. In 2015, she called the story “without merit.” The accounts differ, and the cited coverage reports no adjudicated finding.
description_long: Donald Trump physically and sexually assaulted his wife Ivana Trump during their marriage, with court deposition testimony describing violent rape after painful scalp surgery where Trump pulled out Ivana's hair in rage and forced sexual intercourse while she pleaded for him to stop, demonstrating escalating domestic violence and sexual assault within intimate relationship. The systematic spousal abuse included pattern of physical violence and sexual assault that Ivana described in sworn testimony as 'rape' during divorce proceedings, though she later recanted under pressure from confidentiality agreement that required Trump's permission for any public statements about their marriage. The domestic violence escalated during Trump's affair with Marla Maples, with physical and sexual abuse occurring during period when Trump was publicly humiliating Ivana through tabloid coverage while conducting extramarital relationship that violated marriage vows and family stability. Trump's spousal abuse violated criminal law and constitutional protections by using physical violence and sexual coercion within marriage while creating traumatic environment that included both physical assault and psychological abuse designed to control and terrorize intimate partner. The marital rape occurred during era when spousal rape was illegal in New York State, with Ivana's testimony providing detailed account of violent sexual assault that constituted criminal behavior masked by marriage relationship and later suppressed through legal settlements requiring victim silence. The domestic violence established Trump's foundational approach to intimate relationships and women's autonomy, demonstrating systematic willingness to use physical violence and sexual assault to control partners while using legal mechanisms to suppress victim testimony and accountability for criminal abuse within marriage.
subcategory: Domestic Violence and Marital Sexual Assault

title: Military Force Threats Against Domestic Political Opposition
description_short: Military Force Threats Against Domestic Political Opposition
description_medium: In a 2024 interview, Trump said the National Guard or military could handle people he called “the enemy from within,” if necessary. The Associated Press also reported his proposals to move troops to the southern border and use military forces in deportation operations. In January 2025, he declined to rule out force to take Greenland or the Panama Canal. These reports document remarks and proposals, not a domestic deployment.
description_long: Donald Trump promised to use military force against 'the enemy from within' the United States while suggesting deployment of troops against domestic political opponents, demonstrating systematic preparation for military suppression of American citizens who opposed his political agenda through armed force deployment that violated Posse Comitatus Act and constitutional protections. The comprehensive military threat campaign included Trump's explicit statements about using military against internal enemies while exploring troops for domestic policy priorities including deportations and civil unrest suppression, creating systematic framework for military control over American civilian population through armed force deployment against political opposition. The domestic military deployment extended to promises of military intervention in Middle East and Americas while threatening that 'hell will break out' if political demands were not met, demonstrating willingness to use military force both domestically and internationally to achieve political objectives through systematic armed intimidation rather than democratic processes. Trump's military force threats violated constitutional civilian control and democratic governance by promising systematic deployment of armed forces against American citizens while transforming military from national defense into political weapon used against domestic opposition and constitutional dissent. The military intimidation created unprecedented threat to American civil liberties while demonstrating systematic preparation for military rule that eliminated democratic governance through armed suppression of political opposition and constitutional rights that had historically protected Americans from military control. The domestic force threats established Trump's systematic approach to political opposition and constitutional governance, demonstrating willingness to use military power against American citizens while systematically preparing armed suppression of democratic dissent through military deployment that violated constitutional protections and democratic principles limiting military intervention in civilian political processes.
subcategory: Military Force Threats Against Domestic Political Opposition

title: Hydroxychloroquine Death Push - Deadly Drug Promotion
description_short: Hydroxychloroquine Death Push - Deadly Drug Promotion
description_medium: On June 15, 2020, the FDA revoked emergency authorization for donated chloroquine and hydroxychloroquine from the Strategic National Stockpile to treat some hospitalized COVID-19 patients. The agency said the drugs were unlikely to be effective for those uses and that potential serious cardiac effects meant known and potential risks outweighed benefits. The notice does not link Trump’s promotion to particular deaths or shortages.
description_long: Donald Trump relentlessly promoted hydroxychloroquine as a COVID-19 treatment despite lacking scientific evidence and ignoring warnings from medical experts about the drug's dangerous side effects, leading to shortages for patients who legitimately needed the malaria medication and contributing to preventable deaths. Trump called hydroxychloroquine a 'game changer' and said 'What do you have to lose?' while pushing the unproven treatment at White House briefings, on social media, and in interviews. His promotion was based on a flawed French study and boosted by Fox News personalities rather than rigorous clinical trials. The drug became a political symbol rather than a medical treatment, with Trump supporters demanding access while doctors warned about cardiac risks and other serious side effects. Studies later showed hydroxychloroquine was not only ineffective against COVID-19 but could increase the risk of death in hospitalized patients. Trump's promotion caused a run on hydroxychloroquine supplies, leaving lupus and rheumatoid arthritis patients unable to access their life-saving medication. The FDA eventually revoked emergency use authorization for the drug after studies confirmed it was ineffective and potentially harmful. Trump's hydroxychloroquine push exemplified his pattern of promoting unproven treatments while ignoring scientific expertise, turning medical decisions into political loyalty tests. His 'what do you have to lose?' attitude toward an unproven drug showed his willingness to gamble with American lives based on wishful thinking rather than medical evidence. The hydroxychloroquine disaster demonstrated how presidential medical misinformation could directly harm public health by creating demand for ineffective treatments while undermining trust in actual medical experts.
organization_tags: Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority
U.S. Department of Health and Human Services

title: Trump: Scott Bessent cuts Booz Allen contract to protect himself, Trump, other billionaires
description_short: Trump: Scott Bessent cuts Booz Allen contract to protect himself, Trump, other billionaires
description_medium: On January 26, 2026, TrumpFile reported that Treasury cancelled 31 Booz Allen Hamilton contracts worth $21 million, citing the firm’s connection to an older IRS data leak. Booz Allen said the employee responsible used government systems and that the company held no taxpayer data on its own systems. The article does not establish that Scott Bessent acted to protect himself, Trump, or other wealthy taxpayers.
description_long: On January 26, 2026, TrumpFile reported that the Treasury Department cancelled 31 Booz Allen Hamilton contracts worth a total of $21 million. The article says the decision followed an IRS data leak from more than five years earlier. It identifies Charles Edward Littlejohn, a Booz Allen employee working as an IRS contractor, as the leaker and says he pleaded guilty in 2023 and received a five-year prison sentence. The leaked tax information concerned Donald Trump, Elon Musk, and Jeff Bezos. TrumpFile quotes Booz Allen’s statement that Littlejohn’s conduct involved government systems, that the company stored no taxpayer data on its own systems, and that it could not monitor government networks. The article also reports Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s complaint that Booz Allen had failed to protect sensitive taxpayer information. TrumpFile disputes that explanation and suggests the contract cancellations were intended to shield Bessent and wealthy taxpayers named in the leak. It does not provide evidence establishing that motive or showing that the cancellations changed those taxpayers’ obligations.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Scott Bessent cuts Booz Allen contract to protect himself, Trump, other billionaires
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Scott Bessent cuts Booz Allen contract to protect himself, Trump, other billionaires

notes: needs_context: The linked TrumpFile article reports Treasury’s contract cancellations, the older IRS data leak, Littlejohn’s conviction, and Booz Allen’s response. Its accusation that Bessent acted to protect himself, Trump, or other billionaires is not supported by evidence in the article.
